description: CloudFront distributions must enable origin access control

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an S3 bucket origin with no origin access control identifier and no legacy origin access identity configured.
requirements.rationale: An S3 origin with no restriction mechanism allows direct public access to the bucket, defeating the purpose of using CloudFront for access control. AWS recommends OAC to secure S3 origins.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an S3 bucket origin that references an origin access control resource defined in the same template by its identifier.
requirements.rationale: The S3 origin is properly secured by an in-template OAC resource, satisfying the rule's intent of restricting origin access.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an S3 bucket origin that uses the legacy origin access identity (OAI) mechanism but does not configure origin access control.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, any recognized restriction mechanism (OAI or OAC) satisfies the spirit of the rule, even though OAC is recommended.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an S3 bucket origin whose origin access control identifier is an empty string or otherwise unset.
requirements.rationale: An empty identifier is equivalent to having no OAC attached; the S3 origin remains unrestricted.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an S3 bucket origin whose origin access control identifier does not resolve to any origin access control resource defined in the template.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, the rule requires the identifier to resolve to an OAC resource within the template; a dangling reference is treated as non-compliant.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an S3 bucket origin that simultaneously specifies a legacy origin access identity and an origin access control identifier that does not resolve to any OAC resource in the template.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, the valid OAI provides a recognized restriction mechanism and supersedes the dangling OAC reference.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has multiple origins where every S3 origin has a properly resolved origin access control attached and all other origin types are non-OAC-eligible.
requirements.rationale: All OAC-eligible origins are protected; non-eligible origins (e.g., custom HTTP origins) are out of scope for OAC.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has multiple origins where at least one S3 origin lacks any origin access control or origin access identity, while other S3 origins are correctly secured.
requirements.rationale: Every OAC-eligible origin must be secured; one unprotected S3 origin exposes the bucket and constitutes non-compliance.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has only non-S3 origins that are nevertheless OAC-eligible (such as Lambda function URL origins, MediaStore origins, or MediaPackage v2 origins) and none of them has an origin access control attached.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, all OAC-eligible origin types must have OAC configured; missing OAC on these origins is non-compliant.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an OAC-eligible non-S3 origin (Lambda function URL, MediaStore, or MediaPackage v2) where the origin access control identifier value is provided via an unresolvable expression.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, unresolvable values cannot be asserted as non-compliant on any origin type.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has only origin types that are not eligible for OAC (such as a generic custom HTTP origin pointing at an arbitrary domain).
requirements.rationale: OAC applies to specific origin types (S3, Lambda function URL, MediaStore, MediaPackage v2); generic custom origins are out of scope for this rule.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an empty origins collection.
requirements.rationale: With no origins, there are no OAC-eligible origins to evaluate; the rule has no applicable subject. Schema validity is enforced elsewhere.

requirements.description: A CloudFront distribution has an S3 bucket origin with a properly attached origin access control, alongside an OAC resource configured with a wildcard or generic signing/origin-type configuration that still resolves to a valid OAC.
requirements.rationale: The S3 origin is associated with a recognized OAC resource. The rule checks the presence and resolution of the OAC reference, not the granularity of its internal configuration.
